title: Debugging Workflow
summary: The standard loop for hunting Roblox bugs: read the exact error in Output, locate the script/line, print the suspicious values (or use breakpoints), form a hypothesis, test ONE change, repeat. Reproduce first, fix second.

explanation.whatItIs: A disciplined loop that turns 'it's broken' into 'fixed, and I know why'.
explanation.whyItExists: Random changes rarely fix real bugs and always hide the lesson. System beats luck.
whenToUse: Step 1 — Reproduce: make the bug happen on demand
Step 2 — Read: full error text, script name, line number (Output window)
Step 3 — Inspect: print values / set breakpoints around that line
Step 4 — Hypothesize: 'this is nil because…' / 'this fires twice because…'
Step 5 — Change ONE thing, retest, repeat
whenNotToUse: Shotgun-editing multiple systems at once — you lose the signal
tips: Print TYPE + VALUE: print("coins:", typeof(coins), coins)
Bisect: comment out half the logic to find which half misbehaves
Studio Debugger: breakpoints, watch expressions, call stack
Keep a scratch pad of what you ruled out
commonMistakes: Fixing symptoms (adding random waits) instead of causes
Ignoring the line number — it's usually pointing AT the truth
Testing with 'works sometimes' — non-reproducible means your setup varies

examples.title: Diagnostic prints that pay rent
examples.code:
-- Instead of:  print(part)  → "Part"
print("trap part:", part, part and part:GetFullName())
print("coins type/value:", typeof(coins), coins)

-- Branch tracing:
if canActivate(player) then
    print("canActivate → true for", player.Name)
else
    print("canActivate → FALSE for", player.Name,
          "character:", player.Character ~= nil)
end
